What actually matters in a 1.5 ton AC under ₹45,000

Five years ago, ₹45,000 bought you a basic 3-star non-inverter AC. In 2026, it buys a 5-star inverter split AC with Wi-Fi, AI cooling modes, and a 10-year compressor warranty -- the kind of features that cost ₹70,000+ just two years ago.

The catch: there are now 50+ 1.5 ton ACs in this price range, and most of them are forgettable. We picked the five that aren't. Here's what we looked for, and what tripped up the one model we recommend skipping.

The four specs that decide if a 1.5 ton AC is actually good in 2026: 5-star ISEER (5.0+), copper coils, Wi-Fi control, compressor warranty of 10 years. Noise under 42 dB is a strong quality signal -- a quiet compressor means better engineering. Brand service network matters more than most people realise: a 10-year warranty is useless if the nearest service centre is 200 km away.

If you only buy one thing from this list: get the LG PS-Q19YNZE. It's the only AC in this bracket with 6-in-1 convertible cooling, AI mode, and a 39 dB compressor -- the quietest in the test.

Frequently asked questions

Is 1.5 ton enough for my room?

Yes, for rooms between 120 and 180 sq ft. For smaller rooms (under 100 sq ft) get a 1 ton; for larger rooms (200+ sq ft) get a 2 ton. The right size matters more than the brand.

What is ISEER and what is a good rating?

ISEER is the Indian Seasonal Energy Efficiency Ratio -- higher is more efficient. 5-star ISEER ACs use about 30% less electricity than 3-star. Aim for ISEER 5.0+ in this bracket.

Do I need copper coils?

Yes. Copper coils last longer, cool faster, and are easier to repair than aluminium. Every pick on this list uses copper.

How much electricity does a 1.5 ton AC use?

A 5-star inverter 1.5 ton AC uses about 0.8-1.2 units per hour of active cooling. At ₹7/unit, that's roughly ₹6-9 per hour of use -- or about ₹2,000-3,000 per year if you run it 6 hours daily for 6 months.

Bottom line

If you want the best 1.5 ton AC under ₹45,000 in India, buy the LG PS-Q19YNZE. It's the quietest in the bracket, has the most flexible cooling modes, and LG's service network is unmatched. For coastal cities (Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata), the Daikin FTKM50U's anti-corrosion coating makes it the better 15-year investment. For best value, the Voltas Vectra Elite at ₹40,990 saves ₹2,000 with barely any quality loss. And if you hate cold drafts while sleeping, the Samsung Wind-Free at ₹44,490 is worth the premium.

Installation and running costs

The advertised price is not the price you'll pay. Budget another ₹3,000-5,000 for installation -- copper piping extension (if the indoor and outdoor units are far apart), wall mounting brackets, drainage pipe, and electrician fees. Most brands offer free installation in the box but, but read the fine print: standard installation is 3 metres of copper piping. Beyond that, it's ₹500-700 per metre.

Annual running cost is the hidden factor. A 5-star 1.5 ton AC used 6 hours daily for 6 months will cost ₹2,000-3,000 in electricity. A 3-star AC will cost ₹2,800-4,200 for the same usage. Over 10 years (the typical compressor life), the 5-star saves ₹8,000-12,000 -- which more than covers the ₹5,000-8,000 price premium.

What to do with your old AC

If your existing AC is over 7 years old and still working, sell it on OLX for ₹3,000-8,000 depending on brand. This effectively drops the LG PS-Q19YNZE to ₹34,990 -- cheaper than a 3-star new AC with worse features. If your old AC needs a gas top-up (a common failure after 5-6 years), the repair will cost ₹2,500-3,500 for a one-time fix -- not worth it on an AC that's already 7+ years old. Replace instead.
